title: Rosalind and the Drop
premise: Beatrix Amberdale, a disgraced intelligence analyst working deniable cases, is approached by a stranger named Rosalind Voss who claims Beatrix once saved her life — a favor Beatrix never performed. The debt, Rosalind insists, must be repaid anyway: she carries 'the Drop,' a data cache proving a joint covert operation by three governments murdered civilians and framed a dead whistleblower. As an assassin named Corvus closes in and the extraction flight to asylum looms at dawn, Beatrix must choose between burning what's left of her career and letting the truth die. In the end, Beatrix gets the Drop past three governments by broadcasting it through the one channel no agency dares jam — a civilian weather satellite uplink — while Rosalind sacrifices her escape seat, revealing she was the whistleblower's daughter all along; justice lands publicly at dawn, but both women walk away changed, unclaimed by any flag.
about_author: Odile Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former policy researcher who spent years adjacent to intelligence oversight committees before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people trapped between institutions and their consciences, and lives quietly somewhere with unreliable weather.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Scraping by on unattributable casework in a rain-soaked port city, she is cornered in a noodle bar by Rosalind Voss, who thanks her for saving her life in Prague — an event Beatrix has no memory of. Emotional beat: unease; the past has arrived wearing someone else's face.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. She explains the debt: not repayment, but enlistment. She reveals a fragment of the Drop — coordinates, a date, a body count — and asks Beatrix to authenticate it. Emotional beat: reluctant fascination; Beatrix recognizes the data's fingerprints as real.

chapters.title: Three Flags, One Grave
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Working through the night on borrowed terminals, she confirms the cache matches a buried joint operation called LANTERN GATE. Her old handler warns her off with genuine fear. Emotional beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Seconds
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. The assassin receives his contract: two names, one cache, seventy-two hours. We see his meticulous, almost tender professionalism. Emotional beat: cold inevitability entering the story.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Hiding in a decommissioned lighthouse keeper's cottage, Rosalind and Beatrix plan routes to a journalist contact while counting exits, bullets, and lies. Emotional beat: wary intimacy forming between two women who trust nothing.

chapters.title: What Prague Actually Was
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Digging into her own redacted file, Beatrix discovers why Rosalind believes the favor: her name was forged onto an extraction manifest that never ran. Someone wanted a scapegoat who'd already been discarded. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The First Mistake
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. He finds the safehouse too easily — because Beatrix used an old agency habit to route a message. He watches rather than strikes, waiting for the cache to surface. Emotional beat: the trap tightening without snapping.

chapters.title: The Journalist Who Won't Answer
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Their press contact is found drowned, ruled accidental. Rosalind breaks down; Beatrix holds the plan together by force of will. Emotional beat: grief as fuel; the point of no return.

chapters.title: Auction of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A former colleague offers to sell the Drop's authentication to the highest bidder among three governments. Beatrix realizes the truth itself has become currency. Emotional beat: cynicism confronted — she refuses to play the market.

chapters.title: Corvus Closes
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. He takes Rosalind's courier alive and reads the flight plan: dawn departure from a private strip, seats for two. He lets the courier go, carrying disinformation. Emotional beat: chess, not slaughter — yet.

chapters.title: The Confession at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Rosalind admits the Drop was assembled by her father, the framed whistleblower, and that she has carried it for six years across nine borders. Emotional beat: raw vulnerability; loyalty redefined as inheritance.

chapters.title: Compromised Channels
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Every secure line they test bleeds static that shouldn't be there. Beatrix concludes all three governments already know where they are — and are each waiting for another to act first. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpened into strategic clarity.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Trust
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A tense night conversation: Rosalind accuses Beatrix of being bait; Beatrix accuses Rosalind of choosing her precisely because she's expendable. Neither leaves. Emotional beat: love against duty declared, then denied, then undeniable.

chapters.title: Seventeen Minutes in the Archive Room
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Using a retired ally's credentials, Beatrix physically enters a records annex and copies corroborating documents, tripping a silent alarm with seventeen minutes to spare. Emotional beat: exhilaration — the analyst finally acts.

chapters.title: Corvus's Doubt
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Reading the corroborating files to confirm his targets' claims, he finds his own unit listed among the operation's instruments. His certainty cracks. Emotional beat: the assassin discovers he, too, was spent like ammunition.

chapters.title: The Strip at Midnight
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. They reach the private airfield early, forge the manifest, and find the plane guarded by men from two different governments who don't speak to each other. Emotional beat: absurdity of empire; tension at maximum.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Corvus's POV. Corvus confronts them on the tarmac, weapon raised — then lowers it and hands over his own copy of the operation's orders, asking only that his team's names be included in the record. Emotional beat: the assassin chooses truth over contract.

chapters.title: Dawn Uplink
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. With the flight surrounded, Beatrix executes her real plan: broadcasting the Drop via a civilian weather satellite uplink from the airfield's maintenance shack, beyond any single government's kill switch. Emotional beat: triumph snatched from ambush.

chapters.title: The Empty Seat
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. As sirens converge, Rosalind pushes Beatrix onto the plane alone — her face will be recognized, Beatrix's never was. She stays to stand publicly with the evidence. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the truest form of the repaid favor.

chapters.title: LANTERN GATE Falls Open
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Over forty-eight hours, the broadcast forces resignations, hearings, and a rare joint admission. Rosalind testifies under immunity; Corvus disappears into witness protection he never asked for. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, barely, achieved.

chapters.title: What the Debt Was For
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Months later, reinstated nowhere and employed everywhere, Beatrix decodes the final layer of the Drop: her own forged signature in Prague was Rosalind's father's doing — he'd chosen her years ago as the one analyst who might listen. Emotional beat: awe; the favor always happened, just not yet.

chapters.title: Rosalind and the Drop
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On a neutral shoreline, the two women meet again — Rosalind cleared, Beatrix unburnable now, Corvus's postcard in the mail. They decide the next case together, no flags attached. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; loyalty chosen, not owed.
